dmp.description:
This project investigates the effects of nanoplastics derived from real-world materials,
specifically fishing nets and car tires, on the early life stages of two key benthic
invertebrates: sea urchins and brittle stars. We will quantify impacts on fertilization, larval
development, growth, and survival, and evaluate how these responses can be modulated
by climate change, as projected for the Scandinavian coastal region. Moreover, by
comparing commercial and real-world material nanoplastics, the study will generate
environmentally realistic toxicity data and identify species-specific sensitivities. The
outcomes of this project will fill knowledge gaps on realistic nanoplastic impacts and
multiple stressors effects in marine larvae and provide insights relevant for aquaculture
and ecological risk assessment, supporting better practices for a sustainable blue
economy.
